record.paper_title: Open Problems in Hydrodynamical Approach to Relativistic Heavy Ion Collisions
record.context_brief: Quantitative viscosity effects in QGP hydrodynamics
record.original_question: How can the viscosity of the quark-gluon plasma be analyzed quantitatively and consistently within relativistic hydrodynamics so that the apparently nearly ideal-fluid behavior observed at RHIC can be reconciled with dissipative effects, entropy-density arguments, and the conceptual and technical difficulties of relativistic dissipation?

evidence.quote: The comparison of flow phenomena to the ideal fluid calculation indicates that the emergence of new state of matter which flows like an ideal-fluid at RHIC energies.
On the other hand, Hirano and Gyulassy argue that this is due to the entropy density of the QGP which is much larger than the hadronic phase.

To be precise, a quantitative and consistent analysis of the viscosity within the framework of relativistic hydrodynamics has not yet been done completely. This is because the introduction of dissipative phenomena in relativistic hydrodynamics casts difficult problems, both conceptual and technical.
To extract more precise quantitative conclusion on the ideal nature of the QGP fluid, we should study the effect of dissipative processes on the collective flow variables.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Consider the high-temperature deconfined phase of QCD matter (the quark–gluon plasma, QGP) produced in ultra-relativistic heavy-ion collisions, modelled by relativistic hydrodynamics. In the ideal-fluid limit the energy–momentum tensor is T^{μν} = (e+p) u^μ u^ν − p g^{μν}, with energy density e, pressure p and four-velocity u^μ. Dissipative effects are encoded in additional terms involving the shear-viscosity coefficient η, the bulk-viscosity coefficient ζ, and heat conduction, leading (in a second-order Israel–Stewart-type formulation, needed to avoid the acausality and instabilities of the first-order Navier–Stokes equations) to evolution equations for the shear-stress tensor π^{μν} and bulk pressure Π. A central dimensionless characteristic is the specific shear viscosity η/s, where s is the entropy density.

Observed collective-flow data at RHIC (in particular the differential elliptic flow v_2(p_T) of identified hadrons and integrated anisotropic flow coefficients) are reproduced surprisingly well by ideal hydrodynamics, suggesting that the QGP behaves as a nearly perfect fluid; at the same time, a competing explanation attributes part of this success to the very large entropy-density jump between the QGP and hadronic phases rather than to vanishing viscosity.

Problem. Develop a quantitatively and conceptually consistent formulation of relativistic dissipative hydrodynamics for heavy-ion collisions, and within it perform an analysis that:

(a) gives a causal, stable second-order treatment of shear and bulk viscosity and heat conduction, with controlled initial conditions, equation of state matched to lattice QCD, and a freeze-out / hadronic-cascade afterburner;

(b) quantitatively extracts the temperature-dependent ratio η/s(T) of the QGP from measured flow observables (v_2(p_T), higher harmonics v_n, HBT radii, single-particle spectra) at RHIC energies, with quantified theoretical and experimental uncertainties;

(c) reconciles the apparent ideal-fluid behaviour with the unavoidable presence of dissipation, in particular separating the contribution of a small but non-zero η/s from the contribution of the large entropy-density contrast between QGP and hadron gas as advocated for the suppression of viscous effects at RHIC.

Determine, with rigorous error estimates, the value (or allowed range) of η/s for the QGP and demonstrate consistency of the dissipative hydrodynamic description with the full set of soft-sector observables.
artifact.status_search_result: Since 2006, substantial progress has been made: causal second-order (Israel–Stewart, DNMR) viscous hydrodynamics codes coupled with hadronic afterburners (e.g. VISHNU) and Bayesian analyses have extracted η/s for the QGP, finding values near (1–3)/(4π) with roughly 25% precision. However, sizeable systematic uncertainties remain (initial conditions, bulk viscosity, temperature dependence of η/s, second-order transport coefficients), so a fully consistent and unambiguous quantitative determination is still incomplete.

status_evidence.title: The viscosity of quark-gluon plasma at RHIC and the LHC
status_evidence.snippet: With VISHNU a rather precise (O(25%)) extraction of the QGP shear viscosity (η/s)_QGP from heavy-ion elliptic flow data is possible.
status_evidence.claim: Quantitative extraction of η/s has been achieved at the ~25% level, indicating partial resolution.

status_evidence.title: Hydrodynamic Description of the Quark-Gluon Plasma
status_evidence.snippet: Although theoretical efforts have been successful in reducing the range of η/s, ambiguities remain owing to technical difficulties including initial conditions.
status_evidence.claim: Significant ambiguities remain, so the problem is only partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Viscous Hydrodynamics and the Quark Gluon Plasma
status_evidence.snippet: Data comparison with viscous hydrodynamics indicates η/s < 0.4, preferred range (1–3)×1/4π.
status_evidence.claim: Viscous hydrodynamic frameworks now quantitatively constrain QGP viscosity.
